rows.description: Someone notices another person wearing earphones, hurried or turned away and holds off on starting a chat. Reading cues avoids intrusion and improves the odds of a warm reply.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A person sitting alone is greeted by a stranger and feels relief mixed with wariness. A warm reply and one question back rewards the effort of the person who took the risk.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child simply runs off mid-sentence when something more interesting appears. Learning to say bye or I will go now is a small social skill that adults must model.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child keeps talking, unable to end a phone call with a grandparent. Ending politely needs a signal such as okay, I have to go, and a warm closing phrase.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student at a party says it was great talking, I am going to grab some food, and leaves warmly. A clear positive closing keeps the door open for next time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A person whose colleague ends a chat mid-thought with a glance at the phone feels dismissed. Closure shown with a promise to continue later softens the sting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A listener gently interrupts with a summary and a thanks, then names the next thing they must do. Kind, clear endings protect time without insulting the speaker.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler points at a picture and babbles the sequence of what happened at the park. Recounting begins as fragments, and adults who echo them build language and memory.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child tells an exaggerated story about a huge dog or a flying dream. Imagination and lying are still blurred, and adults can enjoy the story while keeping a gentle line on facts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child hears repeatedly the story of how they were born, how the family struggled or what a grandfather did. Family narratives give a child a place and a sense of belonging.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
